newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa ships first sugar to Saudi refinery.
newsitem.headline: South Africa ships first sugar to Saudi refinery.

text.p: South Africa will ship its first 38,000 tonne raw sugar consignment to a new sugar refinery in Saudi Arabia on Monday or Tuesday, a South African Sugar Association spokesman said.
"The vessel will probably be sailing from Durban either tonight or tommorow morning," he said on Monday.
A further shipment of 34,000 tonnes will follow in July or August to meet current contractual commitments, although industry sources said additional sales to Saudi Arabia were possible.

Saudi Arabia's United Sugar Co started commissioning the kingdom's first sugar refinery at Jeddah in February this year, signalling a shift in the country's traditional buying pattern away from white sugar to raw supplies.
The 500,000-tonne-a-year refinery is 51 percent owned by Saudi Arabia's biggest food group Savola, 15 percent by Tate and Lyle Plc and the balance by Saudi sugar trading firms.
The refinery took delivery of its first cargo of raws from Australia last December.
South Africa harvested its first good sugar cane after five years of drought last year, yielding 2.27 million tonnes of raw sugar, leaving around one million tonnes for export.
For the new 1997/98 (April-March) season industry leaders expect another healthy crop of between 2.3 million and 2.4 million tonnes of sugar.
